open_points.subject: K-02 and A03 sandbox filesystem access
open_points.text: K-02: “no filesystem beyond its input”; A03 rule 1: “a read-only runtime, and one private exchange directory” and rule 4 permits opening paths “inside the exchange directory and the read-only runtime”
open_points.question: May function code inspect runtime files, its own source, directory contents or other non-input files inside the permitted mounts, or must filesystem reads be limited strictly to representations of its declared inputs?
options: Permit reads anywhere in the runtime and exchange directory
Permit only declared input files plus resources needed to load Python
Treat every user-code filesystem access as a sandbox violation
open_points.default_guess: Permit only declared inputs and the minimum runtime files required by the interpreter.

open_points.subject: K-02 and A03 randomness
open_points.text: K-02: “no randomness”; A03 rule 4: “random.Random(seed) with an explicit seed stays usable”
open_points.question: Is deterministic pseudorandom generation allowed in a function, despite the categorical rule that a function has no randomness?
options: Allow explicitly seeded pseudorandom generators
Trap all random-module generation
Treat ‘no randomness’ as meaning only no nondeterministic entropy
open_points.default_guess: Allow explicitly seeded pseudorandom generators and interpret the prohibition as a prohibition on nondeterministic entropy.

open_points.subject: Function determinism
open_points.text: A03 required test 6: “The same implementation on the same input yields the same output digest twice.”
open_points.question: What prevents or classifies nondeterminism from untrapped process and filesystem observations such as process IDs, object-address representations, directory metadata or ordering, interpreter/runtime metadata and similar standard-library facilities?
options: Add traps or fixed values for every nondeterministic observation
Permit them and allow repeated executions to differ
Detect differing outputs by repeated execution
open_points.default_guess: Treat such observations as sandbox violations and fix or trap the relevant interfaces.

open_points.subject: Sandbox process bound
open_points.text: A03 rule 5: “ResourceBounds M04 are enforced from outside the environment with setrlimit (address space, processes)”
open_points.question: Which processes count toward `process_count`: only children created by user code, the Python runner as well, or every process counted by the host user’s `RLIMIT_NPROC`?
options: Count the runner and all descendants in the sandbox
Count only descendants created by user code
Use the host `RLIMIT_NPROC` count even if unrelated host processes affect it
open_points.default_guess: Count the runner and all descendants confined to that execution.

open_points.subject: Authored TrialCase inputs and expected outputs
open_points.text: A04 rule 1: “it is added only when its input values fit the contract version's input ports, its expected outputs, when present, fit the output ports”
open_points.question: Must an authored case supply exactly every input port and, when expectations are present, exactly every output port, or are missing and extra ports or partial expected outputs allowed?
options: Require exact input and output port sets
Require exact inputs but allow partial expected outputs
Allow any subset and ignore extra entries
Refuse extras but allow omissions
open_points.default_guess: Require exactly all inputs and, when `expected_outputs` is present, exactly all outputs, with no extras.

open_points.subject: Try implementation case selection
open_points.text: A04 rule 6: “executes … on the cases … that the request names, all of them when it names none”
open_points.question: Does an explicitly supplied empty case list mean ‘all cases’, ‘execute zero cases’, or an invalid request distinct from omission of the field?
options: Omitted or empty both mean all cases
Only omission means all; an empty list is refused
An empty list executes nothing
open_points.default_guess: Only omission means all cases; an explicitly empty list is refused.

open_points.subject: Disclosure proof on cyclic graphs
open_points.text: A05 checks “disclosure” in phase 8, while “cycles” are checked in phase 7, and A07 defines a function output as “the highest class that can reach any of its inputs”
open_points.question: How is the reachable disclosure class computed for a graph containing a cycle when phase 8 is reached after phase 7 has already found no cycle, and more generally is disclosure computation permitted to rely on the earlier phase having passed?
options: Stop at the phase-7 cycle failure, so phase 8 is never evaluated
Define a fixed-point computation that also works on cycles
Compute classes only for acyclic graphs after phase 7 succeeds
open_points.default_guess: Stop on the phase-7 failure; compute disclosure only after all earlier phases, including acyclicity, have passed.

open_points.subject: Flow reach proof
open_points.text: A05 rule 1 phase 9: “at least one output of every function node reaches, through edges and nodes, a flow output or an operation node”
open_points.question: Is reachability purely structural over all guarded edges, or must the proof account for guard values and reject paths whose combined guard conditions can never be enabled?
options: Use structural reachability and ignore guard feasibility
Use path-sensitive guard feasibility
Count a guarded edge only if its guard can be enabled independently
open_points.default_guess: Use structural reachability over every guarded and unguarded edge.

open_points.subject: Agent submission of personal data
open_points.text: State 0: “the owner alone reads them” and “Personal data values reach an agent only as digest and class”; A12 rule 4: “The owner or any agent may start a run”, while A12 rule 1 accepts supplied flow inputs and M01 permits a flow input of class `personal_data`
open_points.question: May an agent submit literal personal-data values as run inputs, trial-case values or constants, or must those requests be refused because the agent would necessarily possess the value?
options: Agents may send personal data but never receive it from the kernel
Agents may not submit any value declared `personal_data`
Only the owner may start runs or author records containing personal-data literals
open_points.default_guess: Refuse personal-data literals from agents; only the owner may submit them.

open_points.subject: Agent redaction of failure-detail length
open_points.text: A07 rule 5: “returned to an agent only as its length and that class”
open_points.question: Is the reported failure-detail length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points, or characters after replacement and truncation?
options: UTF-8 byte length
Unicode code-point count
Length of the original untruncated body or exception text
open_points.default_guess: Report the UTF-8 byte length of the stored, truncated failure detail.

open_points.subject: Manifest revision reading
open_points.text: M28: “manifest_location`, `manifest_revision`: where the platform manifest is read and the repository revision it is read at”; A08 rule 1: “reads … from `<manifest_location>/<service_id>.json` at the configured `manifest_revision`”
open_points.question: How does the kernel obtain a file at the named revision: read from an already checked-out tree, invoke a repository object reader, verify the working tree revision, or interpret `manifest_revision` in some other way?
options: The host provides `manifest_location` already checked out at that revision
The kernel reads repository objects directly at the revision
The kernel verifies the checkout revision and refuses a mismatch
The revision is informational and the current filesystem file is read
open_points.default_guess: Require the location to be a repository checkout at the configured revision and refuse startup if it does not match.

open_points.subject: Read-operation idempotency_key manifest field
open_points.text: A08 rule 4: “`null` means none; otherwise the text split on `+`” and “For a `read` operation the key is not used and not checked … whatever those parts are”
open_points.question: What happens when a read capability omits `idempotency_key`, supplies a non-string non-null value, or supplies text containing empty or repeated parts?
options: Accept any JSON value and preserve it somehow
Require null or string but skip part validation for reads
Apply the full syntax validation to reads too
Treat a missing field as null
open_points.default_guess: Treat a missing field as null; otherwise require a string or null, while allowing any split parts for a read.

open_points.subject: Acceptance of a changed proposed binding
open_points.text: A08 rule 7: a proposed binding is “checked again by every check of rule 5” and is refused “with `binding_stale` when only the digest differs”
open_points.question: Where in rule 5’s ordered checks is comparison of the current operation digest with the proposal’s pinned digest performed, especially when both the digest and another record or instance condition have changed?
options: Check all rule-5 conditions first, then compare the digest
Compare the digest immediately after locating the operation
Any digest difference takes precedence over every other failure
open_points.default_guess: Run all ordered rule-5 checks first and compare the digest last.

open_points.subject: Path-placeholder input ports
open_points.text: A09 rule 2 requires every path placeholder input schema type to be `string` or `integer`, but at send time the value “must be a non-null string or integer”
open_points.question: Must a placeholder input also have `value` carriage and cardinality `one`, or may a `file` or `many` port pass proposal validation and then fail every invocation’s pre-send check?
options: Require `value` carriage and cardinality `one` at proposal time
Allow other carriage/cardinality and fail at send time
Define extraction of one element or decoding of file bytes
open_points.default_guess: Require a `value`, cardinality-`one` input at proposal time.

open_points.subject: GET and DELETE query inputs
open_points.text: A09 rule 2 allows a query input to be “a list of those sent as a repeated parameter” while M01 independently gives every port cardinality `one` or `many` and A13 says a `many` value is a JSON array of elements matching the port schema
open_points.question: How do schema type `array` and port cardinality `many` combine for query serialization, and are nested lists or a cardinality-`many` port with an array element schema valid?
options: A repeated query parameter comes only from cardinality `many`
A repeated query parameter comes only from a schema of type `array`
Either form is accepted but their combination is refused
Both dimensions may nest and require a defined flattening
open_points.default_guess: Use cardinality `many` for repetition, allow scalar element schemas only, and refuse nested array combinations.

open_points.subject: Multipart part names and filenames
open_points.text: A09 rule 2: `Content-Disposition: form-data; name="<port>"`, with `filename="<port>"` added for a file part
open_points.question: How are quotes, backslashes, control characters, non-ASCII text or other header-unsafe characters in port names encoded or refused when inserted into multipart headers?
options: Restrict multipart port names to a safe ASCII token
Escape quoted-string characters using a specified HTTP rule
Use RFC 5987-style extended parameters
Insert names verbatim
open_points.default_guess: Refuse bindings with multipart port names that are not safe ASCII field tokens.

open_points.subject: Service api_base_url grammar and joining
open_points.text: A08 rule 5 accepts “an absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host”; A09 rule 1 forms the URL from “the `api_base_url` without a trailing `/` followed by the declared path”
open_points.question: Are userinfo, an existing path, query, fragment, percent-encoded host, multiple trailing slashes, IPv6 zone identifiers or other legal URL components allowed, and exactly how many trailing slashes are removed before joining?
options: Require scheme plus host and optional port only
Allow a base path but prohibit query, fragment and userinfo
Accept any absolute URL and use literal string concatenation
Use a standard URL resolver and its normalization rules
open_points.default_guess: Require scheme, host and optional port only, with no userinfo, path other than `/`, query or fragment.

open_points.subject: Plain HTTP loopback exception
open_points.text: A09 rule 4: plain `http` is allowed for “one whose `api_base_url` host is a loopback address”
open_points.question: Does this mean only a literal loopback IP, also names such as `localhost`, or any hostname that resolves to loopback, and how are unusual IPv4 and IPv6 textual forms classified?
options: Only canonical literal loopback IP addresses
Any literal IP parsed as loopback
`localhost` and literal loopback addresses
Any hostname whose current resolution is entirely loopback
open_points.default_guess: Allow only a literal IP address that the standard IP parser classifies as loopback.

open_points.subject: Outbound request size and client limitations
open_points.text: A20 fixes ceilings for surface requests, stored values and service responses, but A09 gives no ceiling for the resulting URL, request headers, JSON body or multipart body
open_points.question: What happens when a valid invocation produces an outbound request too large for the HTTP client, operating system or service transport to construct or send, before the first byte is written?
options: Introduce a fixed outbound-request ceiling
Classify construction failure as the pre-send ‘input cannot be placed’ check
Classify it as `service_unreachable`/`not_sent`
Allow implementation-dependent client limits
open_points.default_guess: Classify deterministic request-construction or client-limit failures as the pre-send ‘input cannot be placed’ refusal.

open_points.subject: HTTP response status outside listed classes
open_points.text: A09 rule 5 classifies only `1xx`, `2xx`, `3xx`, `4xx` and `5xx` responses
open_points.question: How is a syntactically parseable status code outside 100–599 classified?
options: Treat it as a malformed status line
Treat 600–999 as `operation_failed`
Classify by the first digit even outside the listed ranges
open_points.default_guess: Treat any status outside 100–599 as a malformed response.

open_points.subject: Credential and token non-disclosure invariants
open_points.text: A16 rule 7: “No response carries a token [or] a service credential”; A17 rule 2: “The kernel never puts it into the store, a record, a trace, a preview, a failure detail, a log line, a process argument or a response.”
open_points.question: Are these prohibitions about secret provenance or about matching byte sequences? If they are byte-sequence prohibitions, what happens when an owner or agent submits a value equal to a token or credential, or a service returns it somewhere other than the scanned response body?
options: Protect only values originating from protected configuration
Scan and reject/redact matching token and credential bytes everywhere
Guarantee only that the kernel never deliberately copies configured secrets
Refuse any input equal to a configured secret
open_points.default_guess: Interpret the rules as provenance-based: configured secret values are never deliberately copied, while coincidental equal user data is ordinary classified data.

open_points.subject: Data-directory permission check
open_points.text: A18 rule 2: “The directory and everything in it are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise.”
open_points.question: Which ownership and permission modes count as private for directories and files—must all group/other bits be zero as for the configuration file, and are ACLs, hard links and inherited permissions checked?
options: Require ownership by the kernel user and no group/other permission bits
Require only that other users cannot read content
Also reject ACL access and multiple hard links
Rely on successful no-follow opens without checking modes
open_points.default_guess: Require kernel-user ownership and zero group/other permission bits on every directory and file.

open_points.subject: Ordering of operation-output validation failures
open_points.text: A09 rule 3 validates that “each output port takes the member of the same name, which must validate against the port”; A15 rule 4 checks oversized values “per output port”
open_points.question: When several output members are missing, invalid or oversized, which port determines the recorded failure detail and first named reason?
options: Validate output ports in Unicode code-point name order
Use binding declaration order
Report a generic contract violation without naming a port
open_points.default_guess: Validate output ports by Unicode code-point order of port name and report the first failure.

open_points.subject: Run input and trial value size for `many` ports
open_points.text: A12 rule 1 says “each value … is within `stored_value_bytes_max`” and M21 says a `many` value is one StoredValue containing the whole JSON array
open_points.question: Is `stored_value_bytes_max` applied to the canonical bytes of the complete array, to each element separately, or to both?
options: Apply it to the complete array only
Apply it to each element only
Apply it independently to every element and to the complete array
open_points.default_guess: Apply it to the complete array StoredValue; element schemas validate elements but do not give each a separate stored-value allowance.

open_points.subject: Manifest and required-header text bounds
open_points.text: A16 bounds “every other string anywhere in the request”, while required headers and manifest strings come from the manifest and A20 defines no corresponding manifest-text ceiling
open_points.question: What bounds apply to service IDs, operation names, paths, base URLs, required-header names and values, and other manifest text before they are stored, included in previews or sent?
options: Apply `bounded_text_bytes_max` to all manifest strings
Define separate release ceilings for manifest and header fields
Permit manifest strings up to the manifest file or outbound-request limit
Leave the limits to the parser and HTTP client
open_points.default_guess: Apply `bounded_text_bytes_max` to each manifest string.
